overview: This Senate resolution states the Senate's view that Ghislaine Maxwell should not receive a presidential pardon, a shortened sentence (called a commutation), or any other form of clemency. Maxwell was convicted by a federal jury in New York in 2021 of sex trafficking and related crimes involving minors, carried out with Jeffrey Epstein, and was sentenced to 20 years in federal prison. The resolution notes that the President has said he has the power to pardon her and has not ruled it out. It says clemency would go against justice and accountability for crimes against children, and declares that the Senate stands with victims of sexual exploitation and trafficking. As a "sense of the Senate" resolution, it expresses an opinion and does not limit the President's constitutional pardon power. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on July 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say the Senate should speak clearly that people convicted of trafficking children must serve their sentences, and that doing so shows support for victims.
against: Critics say the pardon power belongs to the President alone under the Constitution, so the resolution is a symbolic statement that cannot change what happens in this case.
